Northwind's invoices exported with the wrong tax rate for their Dutch entity, and their finance team only caught it after some had already been sent to their clients — they emailed Marco about it on a Sunday night. [[M1#16]] Diego traced it to the rounding change from August, which only affected accounts with multiple tax jurisdictions — essentially just Northwind. [[M1#17]] Forty-one invoices over two weeks were affected; the calculation fix was quick, but regenerating the already-sent PDFs was the harder part. [[M1#19]]

Resolution:
- Diego fixed the calculation the same day and sent a list of affected invoice numbers by the next morning so Northwind could issue corrections; Marco called their CFO himself. [[M1#20]][[M1#21]]
- Marco told Diego not to promise any credit in the note, deciding after the call. [[M1#23]]
- By September 15 the issue was closed: corrected invoices went out, Northwind's finance team confirmed the numbers, and the CFO replied to Marco's note. [[M2#9]]
- Marco gave Northwind one month free, with Ana applying the credit that day. [[M2#10]][[M2#11]]
- At the retro, Diego cited it as a win: a bad week, fixed in a day, and the customer stayed. [[M4#2]]
